summary: Recommend keeping block-classify.ts's current architecture: an ordered OR-chain of independent, pure, synchronous heuristics. This is the only shape that satisfies all four constraints simultaneously: it is trivially unit-testable with no DOM/mocks (test coverage), it lets each real-world false-negative ship as one small additive function+test (matches the observed 0.1.18/0.1.19 release cadence), it has no threshold or setting to expose (R24, no UI control), and OR-composition is monotonic so no heuristic's positive signal can be cancelled by others (R25, fail-closed to pan). Reject any move toward a scored/weighted/ML classifier (breaks R25's monotonic guarantee, requires an evaluation corpus this project doesn't have per the spec's own Open Gaps), any operator-facing override or confidence knob (direct R24 violation), and any async/stateful/backend classification (breaks R26/R27 content-only stability and reintroduces DOM/timing test costs).
rejected_alternatives: operator-facing override, toggle, or confidence threshold
